newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian industry cheers Chidambaram's return.
newsitem.headline: Indian industry cheers Chidambaram's return.

text.p: Indian business on Wednesday cheered the expected return of former finance minister P. Chidambaram to the government, saying he would quicken economic reforms and relieve foreign investors' anxiety.

"We are confident that the reform process will be carried forward and the economy can look forward to an accelerated growth rate," said Manashi Roy, senior director of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).

Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress party announced late on Tuesday that it would enter Gujral's government. It had said on April 19 that it would remain in the ruling United Front coalition but stay out of the new government.
Government officials said Chidambaram would be sworn in as finance minister later this week.
Share prices on the Bombay stock exchange jumped more than one percent in early trade on news that the party had decided to enter Gujral's government and Chidambaram would return as finance minister.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's index jumped more than two percent within 30 minutes of opening, buoyed by the news. Prices later fell back but remained broadly higher on the day.

"Chidambaram's return would be a very important component of a major thrust forward with the reform process and the pending issues which were his babies would get the right impetus," said Amit Mitra, secretary-general of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI).
Chidambaram is one of the architects of the free-market economic reforms programme that India launched in 1991.
"It is only appropriate that the person who was architect of the budget would be piloting the Finance Bill, and it also reinforces the confidence on India," CII's Roy added.

Parliament convened on Wednesday to consider the 1997/98 (April-March) budget, which Chidambaram presented in February. The plan, which aims to slash income tax and reduce import tariffs, is expected to be passed by May 12.

"We now see the economy back on the rails. With Chidambaram back in the seat, the budget would be cleared without much ado and some of the other policies that he had envisaged would be followed up," said V. Raghuram of the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India.
Gujral has kept the finance ministry portfolio for himself since assuming power last week in the hope that Chidambaram would return to the government.
